newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Lloyds TSB shares delta-hedged by calls.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Lloyds TSB shares delta-hedged by calls.

text.p: The biggest stock UK options trade on Tuesday was a hedged position in Lloyds TSB Group in an otherwise thinly traded market, dealers said.
A hedge was executed when a dealer sold 2,300 December 700 calls in the banking group at 87p and then bought 1.6 million shares at 740p in a volatility trade.
Dealers said the option delta was 0.7 meaning that for every 1p move in the share price the calls will change in value by 0.7p.
In general, if the share price falls sufficiently then the call option premium will also fall.
It may then be possible to make a profit by buying back the original calls and selling calls having a lower strike price -- in sufficient numbers to still render the position delta-neutral.

On the other hand, if the share price rises, the trader may choose to do nothing and risk being assigned the calls -- in which case 1.6 million shares will have to be sold to the call buyer at 740p each.
An alternative will be to "roll-up" the options position by buying back the short calls -- before being assigned -- and selling calls having a higher strike price.
Rolling-up will make an initial loss but offers potential for greater profits if the shares then make a reversal.
By 1505 GMT, Lloyds TSB shares were up 25p to 755p.
